newsitem.title: USA: U.S. interest rate swap spreads tighten a bit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. interest rate swap spreads tighten a bit.

text.p: Spreads on U.S. interest rate swaps narrowed a bit at the short-end, as market participants reassessed the likelihood of a Fed rate hike.
Friday's report of the September producer price index and a revision to August retail sales gave further support to a bullish trend building throughout the week.

While cash markets have rallied, Eurodollars have outperformed pulling swap spreads in, dealers noted. "Euros are up about 25 basis points out a few years," one trader said of the futures market's recent trend. "Treasuries are up but lagging that gain."
On two-year LIBOR swaps, spreads were quoted at 15 to 16 basis points bid, 18 basis points offered, about two basis points narrower than a week ago.
On three-year LIBOR swaps, spreads were quoted at 18 basis points bid, 21 basis points offered, about one basis point tighter than a week earlier.
At the middle of the swap curve, spreads on five-year swaps were quoted at 24 to 25 basis points bid, 27 basis points offered, one basis point tighter.

And at the long end, the market shrugged off the week's auction of new 10-year notes. Spreads on 10-year swaps were quoted at 33 to 34 basis points bid, 35 basis points offered, about one basis point tighter on the offer-side.

Expected Eurobond issuance next week that could be swapped is likely to keep a lid on 10-year spreads, traders said. Heavy swapping by fixed-rate dollar borrowers tends to tighten spreads in the five and 10 year sectors.
